correctness.rationale: This is the complex-symmetric T_3(2), not a Hermitian determinant. Writing d=1−α, log(f/ζ) has coefficients 2dx, dy, and 2dw/3, giving the displayed a_2,a_3,a_4. The determinant factors as (a_2−a_4)(a_2²+a_2a_4−2a_3²). For the nonstandard inequality, take the Schur representation (p−1)/(p+1)=ζω and h=1−|x|². Its first two Schur steps yield y=x²+hu and w=x³+h(2xu−conj(x)u²+(1−|u|²)v), |u|,|v|≤1. Subtracting gives xw−y²=h(−u²+x(1−|u|²)v), hence |xw−y²|≤h. Consequently |6x²+2xw−3y²|≤6|x|²+2h+1=3+4|x|²≤7. Equality forces |x|=1, the Schur function constant, and then |6−x²|=7, i.e. x=±i. The first determinant factor is bounded by (2d/3)(4+3d+2d²) using |x|,|y|,|w|≤1; the second equals (2d²/3)(6x²+2xw−3y²−6dx²y−8d²x⁴). Its bound is (2d²/3)(7+6d+8d²). Both sharp bounds are simultaneous exactly at x=±i: y=−1 and w=−x align the summands. Positivity of d forces equality in the moment estimate if the determinant is extremal. Integrating p gives the two claimed normalized functions. This establishes all real 0≤α<1 without sampling, and at α=0 yields 84.
residual_risks: The class at α=1, higher-dimensional mapping versions, Hermitian determinants, and other coefficient indices are not covered.
